app.name: ForensicGuard
app.backendDownBody: Run <command>python backend/dev.py</command> in a terminal, then try again.
app.privacyLine: Privacy first — no database, no account, no permanent evidence storage.
app.disclaimerLine: Static triage based on indicators and heuristics. Not a definitive malware or phishing verdict.
app.wakeBody: The server goes to sleep after a few minutes without use and has to start back up. The connection happens on its own — there is nothing to do but wait about a minute.
app.wakeFailedBody: We are still trying to connect automatically, now less often. The page unlocks by itself when the server answers — or force a new attempt below.
app.wakeReady: As soon as it is online, the upload area unlocks and you can analyse your file.
app.wakeSlowTitle: This is taking longer than usual

landing.headline: Know what a file really is
landing.subheadline: Forensic triage that inspects files, images and emails without ever opening them.

upload.question: Does this file deserve a closer look?
upload.intro: Drop a file, an image or an email. ForensicGuard inspects it without opening it, gathers objective indicators, and explains every point it assigns.
upload.or: or select a file from your computer

capabilities.imageItems: Dimensions and colour mode|Full EXIF metadata|Camera make and model|Editing software|GPS coordinates
capabilities.emailItems: Headers and Received chain|SPF, DKIM and DMARC|Reply-To and Return-Path checks|Links that hide their destination|Attachments analysed recursively

privacy.title: What happens to your file
privacy.local: It never leaves your machine — the analysis runs on the backend you started yourself.
privacy.noExecution: Nothing is executed. No macro runs, no image is decoded, no address is contacted.
privacy.temporary: It is written to a temporary file with a generated name and deleted when the analysis ends — including when it fails.
privacy.noHistory: No database, no account, no history.

risk.title: Risk score
risk.explanation: Every indicator that fires adds points, capped at 100. Each one carries the evidence that triggered it — a number without a justification is an opinion, not a finding.
risk.scoredIndicators: {count, plural, =1 {# scored indicator} other {# scored indicators}}

charts.scoreCompositionHint: How much each indicator contributed to the total.
charts.artifactsHint: How many of each pattern were recognised inside the file.
charts.entropyMapHint: Entropy of each successive block. A packed or encrypted section shows up as a plateau near 8 — something the overall average hides.
charts.noData: Not enough data for this chart.
charts.severityHint: How the findings break down by gravity.

errors.tooLarge: This file is {size}, and the server accepts up to {limit}. The limit is configurable in backend/.env via MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE.

export.hint: The HTML report is a single self-contained file. It opens in any browser, with no server and no internet connection.

url.neverVisited: The address is dissected, never visited
url.noRequest: No DNS lookup, no certificate check, no page request
url.anatomyHint: Where the address actually leads. Only the highlighted part decides that — everything else is chosen freely by whoever built the link.
url.punycodeTitle: This domain is written in punycode
url.privateHost: This address belongs to a private or loopback network — ordinary internal traffic, not evasion.

sections.pipelineTitle: Five passes over the evidence, and none of them opens the file
sections.hashBody: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 in a single streaming pass. Identifies the file without revealing its contents.
sections.entropyBody: Shannon entropy overall and per block. A packed section shows up as a plateau the average hides.
sections.signatureBody: 33 magic byte signatures. The extension is a claim; the first bytes are the fact.
sections.stringsBody: Readable text in ASCII and UTF-16, then URLs, IPs, paths and references to command interpreters.
sections.scoreBody: 16 rules turn observations into points, each carrying the evidence that triggered it.
sections.detectTitle: Four kinds of evidence, a single risk scale
sections.fileItems: Executable disguised as a document or image|Extension that contradicts the real signature|Entropy unexpected for the detected format|References to PowerShell, certutil and other LOLBins|Embedded URLs, IP addresses and Windows paths
sections.imageItems: Camera make, model and capture time|Editing software left in the metadata|GPS coordinates, with a link to the map|Decompression bombs, caught without decoding a pixel|Dimensions, colour mode and every readable EXIF tag
sections.emailItems: SPF, DKIM and DMARC verdicts as the receiving server recorded them|Reply-To or Return-Path pointing elsewhere|Links that display one address and lead to another|Each attachment analysed recursively, with its own score|The full Received chain, one of the few headers a sender cannot write
sections.urlItems: Credentials hiding the real host before the @|Mixed alphabets, a Cyrillic character inside a Latin name|Top-level domains that collide with file extensions, like .zip|Double extensions such as invoice.pdf.exe|The address dissected part by part, showing where it truly leads
sections.exampleTitle: Every point comes with the evidence behind it
sections.safetyTitle: Built for files that are hostile by definition
sections.localBody: No account, no database, no upload to anyone else. The backend is the one you started yourself, and the evidence is deleted the moment the analysis ends, including when it fails.
sections.noExecutionBody: No macro runs, no image is decoded, no archive is extracted. Files are read in 64 KB blocks, and every parser that touches hostile input is wrapped and bounded.
sections.noNetworkBody: No DNS lookup, no certificate, no page request. Contacting a suspicious address tells whoever built it that it is being investigated, so the analysis stays structural. The one exception is a button you press: resolving a shortener's destination, which says what it costs first.
sections.limitsTitle: What this tool does not do
sections.limitsBody: ForensicGuard performs static triage. It answers whether something deserves a closer look, never whether it is malware. A clean result means nothing stood out, which is not the same as being safe.
sections.limitsItems: Does not run the file in a sandbox|Does not query reputation services|Does not decrypt or unpack archives|Does not replace an antivirus|Does not issue verdicts, only indicators|Does not keep history of what you analysed

meta.title: ForensicGuard — Digital Evidence Analyzer
meta.description: Open-source forensic triage for files, images, emails and links. Hashes, metadata, explainable indicators and a risk score, computed on your own machine without ever opening the file.

redirect.title: Hidden destination
redirect.hint: The address does not say where it leads. Finding out requires contacting it — which tells whoever built the link that it was opened. Nothing else in this tool touches the network.
redirect.incomplete: The chain did not reach a destination

reason.internal_address: A hop pointed at an internal network address and was refused. This is the protection working: following it would turn the server into a way into its own network.
reason.scheme_not_allowed: A hop tried to redirect to something other than http or https, which has no legitimate use here.
reason.too_many_hops: The chain was longer than the limit allows.
reason.loop: The chain came back to an address it had already visited.
reason.timeout: The chain took longer than the time allowed.
reason.no_host: A hop had no host to connect to.
reason.malformed: A hop was not a readable address.
reason.unknown: The chain stopped before reaching a destination.
